artifacts.title: Plain-text workaround search
artifacts.scope: Bounded search for portable text use and image, prose, custom-font, or PUA workarounds.
limitations: Family-level workaround classes do not establish three qualifying examples for any individual record.

artifacts.title: 1980s and 1990s historical visual-gap report
artifacts.scope: Sampled primary manufacturer manuals for historical response-curve and standalone-glyph evidence.
limitations: The bounded sample cannot establish a complete industry lineage or prove absence outside the reviewed manuals.

artifacts.title: Current representation matrix
artifacts.scope: Compared terminology and representation treatments in eight current vendor sources.
limitations: The source set is not a market census, and mutable online documentation may change.

artifacts.title: Band-stop and notch semantic boundary report
artifacts.scope: Tested exact-alias, narrow-subtype, response-region, and product-mode uses of notch and band-stop.
limitations: No reviewed standards-body source supplied a universal numerical boundary.

artifacts.title: Unicode and adjacent-standards overlap audit
artifacts.scope: Reproducibly audited Unicode 17 semantic candidates, visual near-misses, sequences, and IEC 60617 terminology for all four records.
limitations: Later Unicode versions, restricted IEC data sheets, IEC 60417, ISO 7000, and font-by-font rendering were outside scope.

artifacts.title: Current evidence-status synthesis
artifacts.scope: Synthesized project evidence and counterevidence merged through PR 24 without changing record state.
limitations: A synthesis is not an independent source and cannot increase source-independence counts.

artifacts.title: Shelf history, education, trade-media, and community report
artifacts.scope: Compared historical manuals and teaching material, current education, trade media, and practitioner discussion for shelf semantics, representation, text friction, and boost/cut polarity.
limitations: The bounded English-language sample is not an industry census and does not prove absence of portable shelf-glyph use elsewhere.

artifacts.title: Low-shelf and high-shelf vendor semantics
artifacts.scope: Tested whether low-shelf and high-shelf side semantics remain stable across gain sign and compared compact selectors, contextual curves, and text or hardware controls.
limitations: The purposive sample is not a market census and did not inspect running product builds or establish a shared standalone contour.
